sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • Entries stored without an explicit lifetime now expire after an hour instead of a day. A cache flush does not delete keys, it starts a new generation, so the previous ones stayed in memory until they expired: on a shared 128 MB server dozens of dead generations piled up, filled the memory and evicted live data. An hour is enough for the garbage to clear itself.
  • Starting a new generation now writes the counter in the format the legacy `memcache` driver reads. It was stored raw, the drop-in treated it as a miss and restarted counting from one — which brought old keys back into reach.
